As Kerala sizzles, 11 am to 3 pm becomes danger window; What to do, what to avoid
With temperatures soaring across Kerala, the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has issued a comprehensive safety advisory for the public. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned that maximum temperatures on September 8 and 9 could rise 3°C to 4°C above normal. This spike in heat increases the risk of sunstroke, heat exhaustion, and severe dehydration, prompting officials to issue strict guidelines to safeguard public health.
Peak-hour precautions and hydration
a) Avoid direct sunlight between 11 am and 3 pm, when UV radiation and heat levels are highest.
b) Staying hydrated is critical; drink plenty of clean water throughout the day, even if you do not feel thirsty.
c) During peak daytime hours, it is best to avoid dehydrating beverages such as alcohol, coffee, tea, and carbonated soft drinks.
d) Choose light, loose-fitting cotton clothing, wear footwear when stepping out, and carry an umbrella or a hat.
e) Incorporating fresh fruits, vegetables, ORS (oral rehydration salts) solutions, and buttermilk into your diet can also help maintain essential nutrient levels.
Strict rules for schools and children
a) Educational institutions must prioritise student safety by ensuring adequate ventilation in classrooms and providing ample clean drinking water.
b) Given the exam season, water availability must also be guaranteed in examination halls.
c) School authorities and parents must remain highly vigilant. Outdoor assemblies and school events that expose children to direct sunlight should either be rescheduled or entirely avoided.
d) School trips must be planned to ensure children are not exposed to the sun between 11 am and 3 pm.
e) Local body representatives and staff at Anganwadis must also take special care to protect young children from the harsh heat.
Safeguarding outdoor workers and delivery personnel
a) Employers of two-wheeler delivery riders, particularly those delivering online food, must take proactive steps to ensure their staff's safety.
b) Riders should be instructed to wear heat-protective clothing and be allowed regular rest breaks during the critical 11 am to 3 pm window.
c) Construction workers, agricultural labourers, street vendors, and other manual labourers must adjust their shift timings to avoid working under the scorching midday sun.
d) Media professionals and police personnel on duty should also use umbrellas, avoid direct sun exposure, and stay well hydrated.
Caring for vulnerable groups and animals
a) Special attention must be paid to vulnerable populations, including bedridden patients, the elderly, pregnant women, children, and those with pre-existing medical conditions, ensuring they remain indoors during the hottest hours.
b) Livestock should not be left to graze in the midday sun, and pets must never be tied up in unshaded areas. Leaving children or pets unattended in parked vehicles is extremely dangerous under any circumstances. c) Ensure that fresh water is readily available for both domestic animals and birds.
Fire safety and environmental awareness
a) High temperatures increase the risk of devastating fires in marketplaces, commercial complexes, and waste dumping yards.
b) Establishments are advised to conduct strict fire safety audits and implement precautionary measures, while residents near these sites should remain alert.
c) There is also a heightened risk of forest fires; tourists and residents living near forested areas must strictly comply with instructions from the forest department.
d) Given potential water scarcity, the public is encouraged to conserve water and use rainwater harvesting methods where possible.
e) If you or anyone around you feels discomfort or develops a heat-related illness, rest immediately and seek professional medical assistance.

* Dunelm says heatwave weakened its early new fiscal year trading
* Shares fall by more than 10% in early Tuesday trading
* New strategy includes up to 10 annual store openings
* Plan includes removing £100 million costs over three years
Sept 8 (Reuters) - Dunelm warned that its 2027 profit could fall short of market expectations, driving its shares more than 10% lower on Tuesday, after unusually hot summer weather knocked sales at the start of the British homeware retailer's new financial year.
Industry data showed British shoppers cut back on big-ticket purchases such as furniture and household appliances in August in the latest challenge to Dunelm, which sells items ranging from armchairs to kitchenware.
Shares in Dunelm had fallen 10.9% to 790.7 pence at 0723 GMT after the company forecast its fiscal 2027 adjusted pretax profit to be broadly in line with the £211 million ($286 million) reported for fiscal 2026, which ended on June 27.
Analysts were expecting fiscal 2027 profit of between £209 million and £221 million, a company-compiled poll showed.
Dunelm also detailed a new strategy which includes plans to simplify its product ranges and pricing, open up to 10 stores a year over the next three years and refurbish more than 50 existing locations by fiscal 2028.
The new approach under CEO Clo Moriarty, who joined in October 2025, also involves removing about £100 million of costs over the next three years. Dunelm said in a statement it had cut around 8% of roles across its salaried staff in support and distribution teams since the start of the new financial year.
Dunelm, whose share price had fallen by 19.29% so far this year at Monday's market close, is targeting a return to mid-to-high single-digit annual sales growth over the next three years, supported by store expansion and digital investment.
"We prudently assume special dividends pause for the first two years of the programme as Dunelm accelerates change," said Peel Hunt analyst John Stevenson in a note.

Talaado, September 8, 2026 (HOL) - Guddiga Ilaalinta Saxafiyiinta (CPJ) ayaa ku baaqay in si degdeg ah loo sii daayo wariye, Cabdiqani Xuseen Abokor, oo loo yaqaan Baylood, kaas oo ku xidhan Somaliland tan iyo 29-kii Agoosto, isaga oo aan weli si rasmi ah maxkamad loogu soo oogin dacwad.
CPJ ayaa war ay soo saartay 7-dii Sebtembar ku sheegtay in wariyaha loo xidhay kadib markii uu wareysi muuqaal ah ka qaaday abwaanka caanka ah ee, Ismaaciil Yuusuf Cabdi, oo loo yaqaan Jiheeye, kaasi oo gabay ku habaaray Madaxweynaha Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi Cirro.
“Cabdiqani Xuseen Abokor wuxuu ku biiray liis dheer oo saxafiyiin ah oo Somaliland lagu xidhay laguna hayo xaalado shaki leh bilihii u dambeeyay,” ayay tidhi Muthoki Mumo, Isuduwaha Barnaamijka Afrika ee CPJ.
Waxay intaas ku dartay in toban maalmood kadib markii wariyaha la qabtay, aanay wali hay'adaha Somaliland si rasmi ah maxkamad ugu soo bandhigin eedeymaha loo haysto, iyadoo ugu baaqday xukuumada in si degdeg ah loo sii daayo.
Cabdiqani Baylood ayaa 27-kii Agoosto boggiisa Facebook ku daabacay muuqaal wareysi ah oo uu la yeeshay Abwaan Jiheeye. Intii uu wareysiga socday, abwaanka ayaa tiriyey maanso uu digniin ugu dirayay Madaxweynaha Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro), isaga oo ka codsaday inuu wax ka qabto waxa uu ku tilmaamay in si sharci-darro ah looga qaatay dhul oo uu leeyahay.
Maalintii xigtay, 28-kii Agoosto, ciidamada ammaanka ee Hargeysa ayaa ku xidhay abwaanka, sida uu sheegay qareenka wariyaha, Tawakal Ibraahim Maxamed, iyo Ururka Suxufiyiinta Somaliland (SOLJA). Cabdiqani Baylood ayaa isna la xidhay 29-kii Agoosto kadib markii uu ka jawaabay yeedhitaan uga yimid waaxda Dembi-baadhista Somaliland (CID).
Wariyaha ayaa isla maalintaas muddo kooban kasoo muuqday Maxkamadda Gobolka Maroodi-Jeex, waxaana lagu amray in xabsiga lagu sii hayo muddo toddoba maalmood ah inta baadhitaanku socdo. Qareenkiisa ayaa sheegay in Cabdiqani loo qorsheeyay inuu mar kale maxkamadda kasoo muuqdo Sabtidii, balse aan la horgeyn maxkamadda.
Qareenka wariyaha, Tawakal Ibraahim Maxamed, ayaa CPJ u sheegay in sarkaal ka tirsan CID uu si aan rasmi ahayn ugu sheegay in booliisku doonayaan inay Cabdiqani ku soo oogaan laba eedood.
Eedaha ayaa kala ah “xadgudubka sharafta ama karaamada Madaxweynaha” iyo faafinta dacaayad ka dhan ah xukuumada.
Sida uu qareenku sheegay, eedda koowaad waxay xeerka ciqaabta Somaliland dhigaysaa ugu badnaan saddex sano oo xabsi ah, halka eedda labaad ay gaadhi karto shan sano oo xabsi ah. CPJ ayaa sheegtay in ayna jawaab ka helin codsiyo ay faallo uga raadinaysay Madaxtooyada Somaliland, Wasaaradda Warfaafinta iyo Booliiska Somaliland.
CPJ waxay sheegtay in Somaliland ay sannadkii u dambeeyay adkeeysay cadaadiska lagu hayo xorriyadda saxaafadda, iyadoo uu jiro xadhig badan oo loo geystay saxafiyiin iyo shaqaalaha warbaahinta.

SUBANG JAYA: Malaysia expects electricity demand to continue rising as hotter weather increases the need for air-conditioning and cooling, says Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said this in response to a CIMB Securities warning on Monday (Sept 7) that El Niño could put greater pressure on the country’s power system next year.
Akmal said electricity demand was already on an upward trend, driven by population growth and increasingly energy-intensive users such as data centres.
“In terms of the projection for demand on energy, definitely we see a pattern of increase,” he told reporters after officiating the Energy Regulatory Insights 2026 here on Tuesday (Sept 8).
He said hotter weather would increase the need for cooling systems and air-conditioning.
“Definitely the weather or the climate that tends to increase energy demand,” he said.
His remarks came after CIMB Securities said that hotter and drier conditions from El Niño could put greater pressure on Malaysia’s electricity and water systems into 2027.
The research house said El Niño was expected to persist into early 2027 and peak between March and May, potentially lifting electricity demand for cooling while worsening water shortages.
CIMB said Malaysia was particularly exposed as electricity demand was already rising, while about 37% of treated water was lost through non-revenue water.
Malaysia’s peak electricity demand is projected to rise to 33.5GW by 2035 from 21.3GW in 2026, while data centres could account for 31% of Peninsular Malaysia’s electricity demand by then, according to CIMB.
Akmal said Malaysia would therefore need to focus not only on adding electricity supply, but also on managing consumption through greater energy efficiency and conservation.
“Looking ahead, definitely managing demand for energy will become as crucial as managing the energy supply,” he said.
He added that the power system, including the grid and wider infrastructure, would have to be continuously upgraded over the next five to 10 years to remain affordable, safe and sustainable.
